content.value: The Crown Verdict: light the door, then crown the toolkits — Papers for professionals

Barkpark's Paper engine already holds 75 block types, three CI-locked render surfaces, an Excel-class formula engine, live query blocks, and a template lock mechanism — and a human professional can insert 33 of those 75 types. Every profession the wish names hits the same wall before it hits any missing block. So the crown verdict is a two-layer build: Layer A lights the authoring door for all twelve professions at once (full palette, presets, doc-type templates, markdown import, a print answer, and the one-flag playground gate); Layer B crowns Teachers and Data Analysts with deeply designed toolkits whose engine spines are already merged and live, and stages an honest, priced contest for the third crown: scientists versus musicians.

content.value: What we will create — the crown verdict

The mission asked three things: engine ground truth, toolkit anatomy, and a crown. The evidence collapses them into one shape. The engine is not the bottleneck — the door is. Twelve S-tier blocks were built and merged in the last wishlist wave alone, and none of them can be inserted by a human. The reader-CSS debt the potential study flagged is paid (PR #5651). The anonymous form-response endpoint is live (commit 615ff9b51). The template lock mechanism is done (pdd-t1). What remains between Barkpark and 'people feel like using Barkpark for Papers alone' is almost entirely on-ramps, plus two verticals whose toolkits are 90% shipped without anyone having assembled them.

Build in two layers. LAYER A (one epic wave, serves all twelve professions): light the human authoring seam — full-vocabulary insert palette, server default_block parity, section presets, vertical doc-type templates on the pdd-t1 lock mechanism, markdown import wired to the paper ingest seam, a decided print answer, and the anonymous playground gate. LAYER B (one wave per crown): crown TEACHERS (worksheet/quiz/intake toolkit — the engine spine is live, the market is the strongest template-consuming profession that exists) and DATA ANALYSTS (data-notebook toolkit — exists end-to-end today, used twice ever). The THIRD crown is a genuine taste call this paper prices but does not decide: scientists/technical authors (medium cost, wide halo, serves engineers and mathematicians too) versus musicians (highest cost, zero prior art anywhere, the most spectacular possible proof that the quality bar is the attraction).
Layer A — light the door (serves all twelve professions at once)

items.value: 1. Full-vocabulary insert palette.

Expand SLASH_ITEMS and CANVAS_SLASH_TYPES from 33 reachable types toward the 60 parity-locked set. The canvas exclusion of data-bearing blocks (charter D4: 'no useful empty default') is solved by presets, not empty inserts — a chart arrives with demo series, a form with three starter questions, a sheet via a picker flow. Every excluded family gets either a designed default or a designed picker; none stay invisible.
2. Server default_block parity — and fix the silent bug.

blocks.ex has 30 default_block/2 clauses and a catch-all that degrades to an empty paragraph. note, stage, and card are slash-offered today but have no clause — picking them in the per-block editor silently inserts a paragraph. Every palette entry gets a real server default in the same change.
3. Section presets and starters.

task-dc84272db59f8490 (the potential study's recommendation #2) is still open. The canvas command palette already has the compound-insert mechanism (CANVAS_COMPOUND_INSERTS — exactly one entry, cards-grid). Grow it: decision-record, comparison-table, KPI-row, worksheet-section, methods-section.
4. Vertical doc-type templates on pdd-t1.

The lock mechanism is done and proven: a doc type declares a locked initial block set, the editor seeds it, Synthesis.scaffold (synthesis.ex:269) is the server twin, and the paper type already enforces title this way. Ship template doc types per crowned vertical — the machinery costs nothing new.
5. Markdown import at the paper seam.

FromMarkdown.blocks/1 exists, is fail-soft, handles GFM + mermaid + portabledoc fences — and is wired only to Studio chat. The bulldocs ingest controller accepts JSON blocks or legacy HTML only. Wiring the existing converter into ingest (a body_markdown branch) is the single cheapest interop unlock in the codebase.
6. The print answer and the playground gate.

Decide browser print (real, hand-tuned @media print CSS at bulldocs.html.heex:928) as the v1 hand-someone-a-page answer, and ship the anonymous rate-limited playground route (bpb-playground-rate-limit — currently 'considering'; everything downstream of the admin flag is built, tested, and seeds a showcase Paper). Server-side PDF stays a named, separately-priced decision — see Risks.

content.value: Today a Paper can be viewed, emailed byte-identically, and printed by the reader's browser — but nothing can be programmatically exported to .docx/.pdf and nothing imported from them. For lawyers, dentists, and healthcare — professions whose artifact IS the trusted handed-over page — this wall, not any missing block, is the gate. That is why they are not first crowns.
Living data: what 'live' honestly means

The query spine is shipped and disciplined, not promissory: tasks/task-list/task-board/roadmap/task-detail take row queries; chart/heatmap/stat take aggregate queries with a closed vocabulary (groupBy status/label/parent/assignee/priority/phase; day/week/month buckets; count/sum/avg/min/max with only 'priority' whitelisted as a measure; k-anonymity 5; scan cap 5000; fail-closed tenancy). But the substrate is hardwired to type=='task' (query.ex:383) — a paper can watch the task system and nothing else. Sheet embeds are the other living channel and use a third refresh model none of Jupyter/Observable/Evidence has: event-push on save — the sheet is the source of truth, saving fans a fresh snapshot into every embedding paper, drafts write-gated from published embedders (#840). No kernel, no build step, no reader-side compute. The data notebook is therefore honestly a TEMPLATE over live blocks, not a new execution engine — the researched read-side essentials (rendered output + a trust signal) need only one addition: a reader-visible as-of stamp.
Chart reality check:

the chart primitive is line/bars only, linear scale only, everywhere. The annotation layer (regions, refLines, labeled points) exists ONLY on the web/email SVG emitter — the TUI and React renderers silently drop it. No scatter, histogram, box plot, error bars, log scale, or trend overlay exists on any surface. The analyst crown's ≤3 new blocks budget goes here first: annotation parity before new chart kinds.
The market check and the corpus caveat

The template-market census ranks teachers first by a wide margin (TpT: 3M+ materials, 1B+ downloads; Canva Education: 80k+ templates across 800k schools) with general business as the base rate — and flags that for five of the twelve professions (finance, legal, healthcare, dental, music-notation) the dominant template artifact is NOT prose-shaped: it is a spreadsheet model, a fill-in contract, a SOAP form, a score. A prose-template pack alone would miss their demonstrated demand — which the interview's Q2 already answers: new needs become new portable block types. Industrial engineers show no template market anywhere probed — the evidence favors reading that as a warning sign, not an open niche.
The corpus caveat, carried honestly:

the 77.6%-prose figure comes from 471 agent-authored papers. It proves the door is closed (agents use the API and still barely used rich blocks before the wishlist wave); it cannot prove what human professionals will do. There is no human-professional usage data anywhere in the system. The teacher and analyst crowns rest on external market evidence precisely because the internal corpus cannot carry that weight.

content.value: Risks and open judgment calls

Every toolkit this paper designs assumes a professional can reach a shareable public Paper URL quickly and freely. Today they cannot: the playground is one admin flag from anonymous, and the only free cloud path (trial signup) leads to a control-plane account, not a Paper. Flipping the flag is cheap; deciding WHERE the individual professional permanently lives (shared playground with TTL? a free papers-only tier? the $69/mo instance?) is a product decision outside this repo's code. If that decision is not made, the toolkits polish a door nobody can walk through.

items.value: Corpus evidence may not transfer.

All internal usage data is agent-authored. The crowns hedge with external market evidence, but no one has watched a real teacher or analyst author a Paper. The flagship showcase papers should double as the first usability instrument.
Print may not be enough.

Browser print CSS is real and good, but 'hand someone a page' for a lawyer or dentist may require server-side PDF (a Chromium-shaped dependency this codebase has deliberately avoided — zero PDF libs anywhere). Recommendation: ship v1 on browser print, and treat server PDF as its own priced decision when a trust-artifact vertical is crowned. The browser-print path has never been proven end-to-end with a rendered artifact — cheap to do, should be done early.
Data-bearing defaults are a design problem, not a registry problem.

Charter D4 excluded chart/stats/sheet from canvas insert for a reason: an empty chart is useless. The palette expansion succeeds only if every data-bearing family gets a designed preset or picker — this is the hard 20% of Layer A.
Freshness stamps vs byte-stable goldens.

An as-of stamp on sheet embeds changes rendered bytes over time, colliding with the golden-locked parity harness and the byte-stability doctrine. Same underlying question as notation's external-grammar debate and citations' one-formatter debate: may the server pre-resolve? Flagged to the capstone; this paper's designs assume TaskResolver-style resolve-at-render, which the doctrine already blesses.
Concurrent-session hazard for the build epic.

The working tree provably lags origin/main during investigation runs; two lanes' absence-claims were voided by it. The build epic must read and branch from origin/main and re-verify the '33' and the open task statuses at wave start — this repo moves daily.

content.value: What we will create — the crown verdict

The mission asked three things: engine ground truth, toolkit anatomy, and a crown. The evidence collapses them into one shape. The engine is not the bottleneck — the door is. Twelve S-tier blocks were built and merged in the last wishlist wave alone, and none of them can be inserted by a human. The reader-CSS debt the potential study flagged is paid (PR #5651). The anonymous form-response endpoint is live (commit 615ff9b51). The template lock mechanism is done (pdd-t1). What remains between Barkpark and 'people feel like using Barkpark for Papers alone' is almost entirely on-ramps, plus two verticals whose toolkits are 90% shipped without anyone having assembled them.

Build in two layers. LAYER A (one epic wave, serves all twelve professions): light the human authoring seam — full-vocabulary insert palette, server default_block parity, section presets, vertical doc-type templates on the pdd-t1 lock mechanism, markdown import wired to the paper ingest seam, a decided print answer, and the anonymous playground gate. For lawyers, dentists, and healthcare — professions whose artifact IS the trusted handed-over page — this wall, not any missing block, is the gate. That is why they are not first crowns.
Living data: what 'live' honestly means

The query spine is shipped and disciplined, not promissory: tasks/task-list/task-board/roadmap/task-detail take row queries; chart/heatmap/stat take aggregate queries with a closed vocabulary (groupBy status/label/parent/assignee/priority/phase; day/week/month buckets; count/sum/avg/min/max with only 'priority' whitelisted as a measure; k-anonymity 5; scan cap 5000; fail-closed tenancy). But the substrate is hardwired to type=='task' (query.ex:383) — a paper can watch the task system and nothing else. Sheet embeds are the other living channel and use a third refresh model none of Jupyter/Observable/Evidence has: event-push on save — the sheet is the source of truth, saving fans a fresh snapshot into every embedding paper, drafts write-gated from published embedders (#840). No kernel, no build step, no reader-side compute. The data notebook is therefore honestly a TEMPLATE over live blocks, not a new execution engine — the researched read-side essentials (rendered output + a trust signal) need only one addition: a reader-visible as-of stamp.
Chart reality check:

the chart primitive is line/bars only, linear scale only, everywhere. The annotation layer (regions, refLines, labeled points) exists ONLY on the web/email SVG emitter — the TUI and React renderers silently drop it. No scatter, histogram, box plot, error bars, log scale, or trend overlay exists on any surface. The analyst crown's ≤3 new blocks budget goes here first: annotation parity before new chart kinds.
The market check and the corpus caveat

The template-market census ranks teachers first by a wide margin (TpT: 3M+ materials, 1B+ downloads; Canva Education: 80k+ templates across 800k schools) with general business as the base rate — and flags that for five of the twelve professions (finance, legal, healthcare, dental, music-notation) the dominant template artifact is NOT prose-shaped: it is a spreadsheet model, a fill-in contract, a SOAP form, a score. A prose-template pack alone would miss their demonstrated demand — which the interview's Q2 already answers: new needs become new portable block types. Industrial engineers show no template market anywhere probed — the evidence favors reading that as a warning sign, not an open niche.
The corpus caveat, carried honestly:

the 77.6%-prose figure comes from 471 agent-authored papers. It proves the door is closed (agents use the API and still barely used rich blocks before the wishlist wave); it cannot prove what human professionals will do. There is no human-professional usage data anywhere in the system. The teacher and analyst crowns rest on external market evidence precisely because the internal corpus cannot carry that weight.

content.value: Risks and open judgment calls

Every toolkit this paper designs assumes a professional can reach a shareable public Paper URL quickly and freely. Today they cannot: the playground is one admin flag from anonymous, and the only free cloud path (trial signup) leads to a control-plane account, not a Paper. Flipping the flag is cheap; deciding WHERE the individual professional permanently lives (shared playground with TTL? a free papers-only tier? the $69/mo instance?) is a product decision outside this repo's code. If that decision is not made, the toolkits polish a door nobody can walk through.

items.value: Corpus evidence may not transfer.

All internal usage data is agent-authored. The crowns hedge with external market evidence, but no one has watched a real teacher or analyst author a Paper. The flagship showcase papers should double as the first usability instrument.
Print may not be enough.

Browser print CSS is real and good, but 'hand someone a page' for a lawyer or dentist may require server-side PDF (a Chromium-shaped dependency this codebase has deliberately avoided — zero PDF libs anywhere). Recommendation: ship v1 on browser print, and treat server PDF as its own priced decision when a trust-artifact vertical is crowned. The browser-print path has never been proven end-to-end with a rendered artifact — cheap to do, should be done early.
Data-bearing defaults are a design problem, not a registry problem.

Charter D4 excluded chart/stats/sheet from canvas insert for a reason: an empty chart is useless. The palette expansion succeeds only if every data-bearing family gets a designed preset or picker — this is the hard 20% of Layer A.
Freshness stamps vs byte-stable goldens.

An as-of stamp on sheet embeds changes rendered bytes over time, colliding with the golden-locked parity harness and the byte-stability doctrine. Same underlying question as notation's external-grammar debate and citations' one-formatter debate: may the server pre-resolve? Flagged to the capstone; this paper's designs assume TaskResolver-style resolve-at-render, which the doctrine already blesses.
Concurrent-session hazard for the build epic.

The working tree provably lags origin/main during investigation runs; two lanes' absence-claims were voided by it. The build epic must read and branch from origin/main and re-verify the '33' and the open task statuses at wave start — this repo moves daily.

The Crown Verdict: light the door, then crown the toolkits — Papers for professionals

Barkpark's Paper engine already holds 75 block types, three CI-locked render surfaces, an Excel-class formula engine, live query blocks, and a template lock mechanism — and a human professional can insert 33 of those 75 types. Every profession the wish names hits the same wall before it hits any missing block. So the crown verdict is a two-layer build: Layer A lights the authoring door for all twelve professions at once (full palette, presets, doc-type templates, markdown import, a print answer, and the one-flag playground gate); Layer B crowns Teachers and Data Analysts with deeply designed toolkits whose engine spines are already merged and live, and stages an honest, priced contest for the third crown: scientists versus musicians.

What we will create — the crown verdict

The mission asked three things: engine ground truth, toolkit anatomy, and a crown. The evidence collapses them into one shape. The engine is not the bottleneck — the door is. Twelve S-tier blocks were built and merged in the last wishlist wave alone, and none of them can be inserted by a human. The reader-CSS debt the potential study flagged is paid (PR #5651). The anonymous form-response endpoint is live (commit 615ff9b51). The template lock mechanism is done (pdd-t1). What remains between Barkpark and 'people feel like using Barkpark for Papers alone' is almost entirely on-ramps, plus two verticals whose toolkits are 90% shipped without anyone having assembled them.

The verdict
Build in two layers. LAYER A (one epic wave, serves all twelve professions): light the human authoring seam — full-vocabulary insert palette, server default_block parity, section presets, vertical doc-type templates on the pdd-t1 lock mechanism, markdown import wired to the paper ingest seam, a decided print answer, and the anonymous playground gate. LAYER B (one wave per crown): crown TEACHERS (worksheet/quiz/intake toolkit — the engine spine is live, the market is the strongest template-consuming profession that exists) and DATA ANALYSTS (data-notebook toolkit — exists end-to-end today, used twice ever). The THIRD crown is a genuine taste call this paper prices but does not decide: scientists/technical authors (medium cost, wide halo, serves engineers and mathematicians too) versus musicians (highest cost, zero prior art anywhere, the most spectacular possible proof that the quality bar is the attraction).

Layer A — light the door (serves all twelve professions at once)

  • 1. Full-vocabulary insert palette. Expand SLASH_ITEMS and CANVAS_SLASH_TYPES from 33 reachable types toward the 60 parity-locked set. The canvas exclusion of data-bearing blocks (charter D4: 'no useful empty default') is solved by presets, not empty inserts — a chart arrives with demo series, a form with three starter questions, a sheet via a picker flow. Every excluded family gets either a designed default or a designed picker; none stay invisible.
  • 2. Server default_block parity — and fix the silent bug. blocks.ex has 30 default_block/2 clauses and a catch-all that degrades to an empty paragraph. note, stage, and card are slash-offered today but have no clause — picking them in the per-block editor silently inserts a paragraph. Every palette entry gets a real server default in the same change.
  • 3. Section presets and starters. task-dc84272db59f8490 (the potential study's recommendation #2) is still open. The canvas command palette already has the compound-insert mechanism (CANVAS_COMPOUND_INSERTS — exactly one entry, cards-grid). Grow it: decision-record, comparison-table, KPI-row, worksheet-section, methods-section.
  • 4. Vertical doc-type templates on pdd-t1. The lock mechanism is done and proven: a doc type declares a locked initial block set, the editor seeds it, Synthesis.scaffold (synthesis.ex:269) is the server twin, and the paper type already enforces title this way. Ship template doc types per crowned vertical — the machinery costs nothing new.
  • 5. Markdown import at the paper seam. FromMarkdown.blocks/1 exists, is fail-soft, handles GFM + mermaid + portabledoc fences — and is wired only to Studio chat. The bulldocs ingest controller accepts JSON blocks or legacy HTML only. Wiring the existing converter into ingest (a body_markdown branch) is the single cheapest interop unlock in the codebase.
  • 6. The print answer and the playground gate. Decide browser print (real, hand-tuned @media print CSS at bulldocs.html.heex:928) as the v1 hand-someone-a-page answer, and ship the anonymous rate-limited playground route (bpb-playground-rate-limit — currently 'considering'; everything downstream of the admin flag is built, tested, and seeds a showcase Paper). Server-side PDF stays a named, separately-priced decision — see Risks.

Why Layer A first is not a taste call: the potential study's diagnosis is evidence-ordered — discoverability > authoring cost > delivery debt — and the third cause is now fixed, which promotes the first two. 71 drift-spelled list blocks in production prove authors reach for names they cannot discover. The engine:door ratio (75:33) is measured, not felt. And Layer A is also the cheap half: it is registry entries, default clauses, one controller branch, and one router pipeline — no new renderers, no new goldens, no doctrine questions.

The notation-typesetting lane's paper carries the full dossier.

Recommendation: crown scientists/technical authors third, on evidence: medium cost, live spines to extend, a competitor dead zone to own, and a halo that covers three more of the wish's named professions (engineers, mathematicians, industrial engineers). Hold musicians as the deliberate flagship-spectacle option — if the user wants the loudest possible statement of the quality bar, that is a legitimate choice this paper cannot make for them. It is taste, and the user owns taste.

The professions this shape deliberately does not crown: engineers are largely served by Layer A alone — the dev family (code-tabs, api-endpoint, diff, filetree, terminal, diagram) is already built and merely unreachable; their documented Confluence exodus is an on-ramps-and-quality story, not a new-blocks story. Lawyers, healthcare, and dentists are gated on trust artifacts (server PDF fidelity, signatures, redaction, regulatory posture) that the atlas and evidence lanes scope — real, but not feasibility-cheap, and wrong as a first crown under zero-setup individual onboarding. Their intake-form needs, meanwhile, ride the Teachers toolkit's form work for free.

Today a Paper can be viewed, emailed byte-identically, and printed by the reader's browser — but nothing can be programmatically exported to .docx/.pdf and nothing imported from them. For lawyers, dentists, and healthcare — professions whose artifact IS the trusted handed-over page — this wall, not any missing block, is the gate. That is why they are not first crowns.

Living data: what 'live' honestly means

The query spine is shipped and disciplined, not promissory: tasks/task-list/task-board/roadmap/task-detail take row queries; chart/heatmap/stat take aggregate queries with a closed vocabulary (groupBy status/label/parent/assignee/priority/phase; day/week/month buckets; count/sum/avg/min/max with only 'priority' whitelisted as a measure; k-anonymity 5; scan cap 5000; fail-closed tenancy). But the substrate is hardwired to type=='task' (query.ex:383) — a paper can watch the task system and nothing else. Sheet embeds are the other living channel and use a third refresh model none of Jupyter/Observable/Evidence has: event-push on save — the sheet is the source of truth, saving fans a fresh snapshot into every embedding paper, drafts write-gated from published embedders (#840). No kernel, no build step, no reader-side compute. The data notebook is therefore honestly a TEMPLATE over live blocks, not a new execution engine — the researched read-side essentials (rendered output + a trust signal) need only one addition: a reader-visible as-of stamp.

Chart reality check: the chart primitive is line/bars only, linear scale only, everywhere. The annotation layer (regions, refLines, labeled points) exists ONLY on the web/email SVG emitter — the TUI and React renderers silently drop it. No scatter, histogram, box plot, error bars, log scale, or trend overlay exists on any surface. The analyst crown's ≤3 new blocks budget goes here first: annotation parity before new chart kinds.

The market check and the corpus caveat

The template-market census ranks teachers first by a wide margin (TpT: 3M+ materials, 1B+ downloads; Canva Education: 80k+ templates across 800k schools) with general business as the base rate — and flags that for five of the twelve professions (finance, legal, healthcare, dental, music-notation) the dominant template artifact is NOT prose-shaped: it is a spreadsheet model, a fill-in contract, a SOAP form, a score. A prose-template pack alone would miss their demonstrated demand — which the interview's Q2 already answers: new needs become new portable block types. Industrial engineers show no template market anywhere probed — the evidence favors reading that as a warning sign, not an open niche.

The corpus caveat, carried honestly: the 77.6%-prose figure comes from 471 agent-authored papers. It proves the door is closed (agents use the API and still barely used rich blocks before the wishlist wave); it cannot prove what human professionals will do. There is no human-professional usage data anywhere in the system. The teacher and analyst crowns rest on external market evidence precisely because the internal corpus cannot carry that weight.

Risks and open judgment calls

The adoption keystone
Every toolkit this paper designs assumes a professional can reach a shareable public Paper URL quickly and freely. Today they cannot: the playground is one admin flag from anonymous, and the only free cloud path (trial signup) leads to a control-plane account, not a Paper. Flipping the flag is cheap; deciding WHERE the individual professional permanently lives (shared playground with TTL? a free papers-only tier? the $69/mo instance?) is a product decision outside this repo's code. If that decision is not made, the toolkits polish a door nobody can walk through.
  • Corpus evidence may not transfer. All internal usage data is agent-authored. The crowns hedge with external market evidence, but no one has watched a real teacher or analyst author a Paper. The flagship showcase papers should double as the first usability instrument.
  • Print may not be enough. Browser print CSS is real and good, but 'hand someone a page' for a lawyer or dentist may require server-side PDF (a Chromium-shaped dependency this codebase has deliberately avoided — zero PDF libs anywhere). Recommendation: ship v1 on browser print, and treat server PDF as its own priced decision when a trust-artifact vertical is crowned. The browser-print path has never been proven end-to-end with a rendered artifact — cheap to do, should be done early.
  • Data-bearing defaults are a design problem, not a registry problem. Charter D4 excluded chart/stats/sheet from canvas insert for a reason: an empty chart is useless. The palette expansion succeeds only if every data-bearing family gets a designed preset or picker — this is the hard 20% of Layer A.
  • Freshness stamps vs byte-stable goldens. An as-of stamp on sheet embeds changes rendered bytes over time, colliding with the golden-locked parity harness and the byte-stability doctrine. Same underlying question as notation's external-grammar debate and citations' one-formatter debate: may the server pre-resolve? Flagged to the capstone; this paper's designs assume TaskResolver-style resolve-at-render, which the doctrine already blesses.
  • Concurrent-session hazard for the build epic. The working tree provably lags origin/main during investigation runs; two lanes' absence-claims were voided by it. The build epic must read and branch from origin/main and re-verify the '33' and the open task statuses at wave start — this repo moves daily.

Left explicitly to the user

  • 1. The third crown: scientists/technical authors (evidence-favored) versus musicians (spectacle-favored). Taste; priced above.
  • 2. The print answer: is browser print-to-PDF acceptable for v1 professional handoff, or is server PDF a hard requirement?
  • 3. Where the individual professional lives: anonymous playground (TTL'd), a new free papers-only tier, or the paid instance — the zero-setup promise cannot be met by any current route without this call.
  • 4. The toolkit mental model: this paper defines toolkit = templates + presets + seeded flagship + ≤3 blocks + interop answer, all on existing machinery. If the user imagines something more app-like (a per-vertical Studio mode), that is an architecture conversation to have BEFORE wave 3.

What we will create — the crown verdict

The mission asked three things: engine ground truth, toolkit anatomy, and a crown. The evidence collapses them into one shape. The engine is not the bottleneck — the door is. Twelve S-tier blocks were built and merged in the last wishlist wave alone, and none of them can be inserted by a human. The reader-CSS debt the potential study flagged is paid (PR #5651). The anonymous form-response endpoint is live (commit 615ff9b51). The template lock mechanism is done (pdd-t1). What remains between Barkpark and 'people feel like using Barkpark for Papers alone' is almost entirely on-ramps, plus two verticals whose toolkits are 90% shipped without anyone having assembled them.

The verdict Build in two layers. LAYER A (one epic wave, serves all twelve professions): light the human authoring seam — full-vocabulary insert palette, server default_block parity, section presets, vertical doc-type templates on the pdd-t1 lock mechanism, markdown import wired to the paper ingest seam, a decided print answer, and the anonymous playground gate. The THIRD crown is a genuine taste call this paper prices but does not decide: scientists/technical authors (medium cost, wide halo, serves engineers and mathematicians too) versus musicians (highest cost, zero prior art anywhere, the most spectacular possible proof that the quality bar is the attraction).

Layer A — light the door (serves all twelve professions at once)

  • 1. Full-vocabulary insert palette. Expand SLASH_ITEMS and CANVAS_SLASH_TYPES from 33 reachable types toward the 60 parity-locked set. The canvas exclusion of data-bearing blocks (charter D4: 'no useful empty default') is solved by presets, not empty inserts — a chart arrives with demo series, a form with three starter questions, a sheet via a picker flow. Every excluded family gets either a designed default or a designed picker; none stay invisible.
  • 2. Server default_block parity — and fix the silent bug. blocks.ex has 30 default_block/2 clauses and a catch-all that degrades to an empty paragraph. note, stage, and card are slash-offered today but have no clause — picking them in the per-block editor silently inserts a paragraph. Every palette entry gets a real server default in the same change.
  • 3. Section presets and starters. task-dc84272db59f8490 (the potential study's recommendation #2) is still open. The canvas command palette already has the compound-insert mechanism (CANVAS_COMPOUND_INSERTS — exactly one entry, cards-grid). Grow it: decision-record, comparison-table, KPI-row, worksheet-section, methods-section.
  • 4. Vertical doc-type templates on pdd-t1. The lock mechanism is done and proven: a doc type declares a locked initial block set, the editor seeds it, Synthesis.scaffold (synthesis.ex:269) is the server twin, and the paper type already enforces title this way. Ship template doc types per crowned vertical — the machinery costs nothing new.
  • 5. Markdown import at the paper seam. FromMarkdown.blocks/1 exists, is fail-soft, handles GFM + mermaid + portabledoc fences — and is wired only to Studio chat. The bulldocs ingest controller accepts JSON blocks or legacy HTML only. Wiring the existing converter into ingest (a body_markdown branch) is the single cheapest interop unlock in the codebase.
  • 6. The print answer and the playground gate. Decide browser print (real, hand-tuned @media print CSS at bulldocs.html.heex:928) as the v1 hand-someone-a-page answer, and ship the anonymous rate-limited playground route (bpb-playground-rate-limit — currently 'considering'; everything downstream of the admin flag is built, tested, and seeds a showcase Paper). Server-side PDF stays a named, separately-priced decision — see Risks.

Why Layer A first is not a taste call: the potential study's diagnosis is evidence-ordered — discoverability > authoring cost > delivery debt — and the third cause is now fixed, which promotes the first two. 71 drift-spelled list blocks in production prove authors reach for names they cannot discover. The engine:door ratio (75:33) is measured, not felt. And Layer A is also the cheap half: it is registry entries, default clauses, one controller branch, and one router pipeline — no new renderers, no new goldens, no doctrine questions.

Living data: what 'live' honestly means

The query spine is shipped and disciplined, not promissory: tasks/task-list/task-board/roadmap/task-detail take row queries; chart/heatmap/stat take aggregate queries with a closed vocabulary (groupBy status/label/parent/assignee/priority/phase; day/week/month buckets; count/sum/avg/min/max with only 'priority' whitelisted as a measure; k-anonymity 5; scan cap 5000; fail-closed tenancy). But the substrate is hardwired to type=='task' (query.ex:383) — a paper can watch the task system and nothing else. Sheet embeds are the other living channel and use a third refresh model none of Jupyter/Observable/Evidence has: event-push on save — the sheet is the source of truth, saving fans a fresh snapshot into every embedding paper, drafts write-gated from published embedders (#840). No kernel, no build step, no reader-side compute. The data notebook is therefore honestly a TEMPLATE over live blocks, not a new execution engine — the researched read-side essentials (rendered output + a trust signal) need only one addition: a reader-visible as-of stamp.

Chart reality check: the chart primitive is line/bars only, linear scale only, everywhere. The annotation layer (regions, refLines, labeled points) exists ONLY on the web/email SVG emitter — the TUI and React renderers silently drop it. No scatter, histogram, box plot, error bars, log scale, or trend overlay exists on any surface. The analyst crown's ≤3 new blocks budget goes here first: annotation parity before new chart kinds.

The market check and the corpus caveat

The template-market census ranks teachers first by a wide margin (TpT: 3M+ materials, 1B+ downloads; Canva Education: 80k+ templates across 800k schools) with general business as the base rate — and flags that for five of the twelve professions (finance, legal, healthcare, dental, music-notation) the dominant template artifact is NOT prose-shaped: it is a spreadsheet model, a fill-in contract, a SOAP form, a score. A prose-template pack alone would miss their demonstrated demand — which the interview's Q2 already answers: new needs become new portable block types. Industrial engineers show no template market anywhere probed — the evidence favors reading that as a warning sign, not an open niche.

The corpus caveat, carried honestly: the 77.6%-prose figure comes from 471 agent-authored papers. It proves the door is closed (agents use the API and still barely used rich blocks before the wishlist wave); it cannot prove what human professionals will do. There is no human-professional usage data anywhere in the system. The teacher and analyst crowns rest on external market evidence precisely because the internal corpus cannot carry that weight.

Risks and open judgment calls

The adoption keystone Every toolkit this paper designs assumes a professional can reach a shareable public Paper URL quickly and freely. Today they cannot: the playground is one admin flag from anonymous, and the only free cloud path (trial signup) leads to a control-plane account, not a Paper. Flipping the flag is cheap; deciding WHERE the individual professional permanently lives (shared playground with TTL? a free papers-only tier? the $69/mo instance?) is a product decision outside this repo's code. If that decision is not made, the toolkits polish a door nobody can walk through.
  • Corpus evidence may not transfer. All internal usage data is agent-authored. The crowns hedge with external market evidence, but no one has watched a real teacher or analyst author a Paper. The flagship showcase papers should double as the first usability instrument.
  • Print may not be enough. Browser print CSS is real and good, but 'hand someone a page' for a lawyer or dentist may require server-side PDF (a Chromium-shaped dependency this codebase has deliberately avoided — zero PDF libs anywhere). Recommendation: ship v1 on browser print, and treat server PDF as its own priced decision when a trust-artifact vertical is crowned. The browser-print path has never been proven end-to-end with a rendered artifact — cheap to do, should be done early.
  • Data-bearing defaults are a design problem, not a registry problem. Charter D4 excluded chart/stats/sheet from canvas insert for a reason: an empty chart is useless. The palette expansion succeeds only if every data-bearing family gets a designed preset or picker — this is the hard 20% of Layer A.
  • Freshness stamps vs byte-stable goldens. An as-of stamp on sheet embeds changes rendered bytes over time, colliding with the golden-locked parity harness and the byte-stability doctrine. Same underlying question as notation's external-grammar debate and citations' one-formatter debate: may the server pre-resolve? Flagged to the capstone; this paper's designs assume TaskResolver-style resolve-at-render, which the doctrine already blesses.
  • Concurrent-session hazard for the build epic. The working tree provably lags origin/main during investigation runs; two lanes' absence-claims were voided by it. The build epic must read and branch from origin/main and re-verify the '33' and the open task statuses at wave start — this repo moves daily.

Left explicitly to the user

  • 1. The third crown: scientists/technical authors (evidence-favored) versus musicians (spectacle-favored). Taste; priced above.
  • 2. The print answer: is browser print-to-PDF acceptable for v1 professional handoff, or is server PDF a hard requirement?
  • 3. Where the individual professional lives: anonymous playground (TTL'd), a new free papers-only tier, or the paid instance — the zero-setup promise cannot be met by any current route without this call.
  • 4. The toolkit mental model: this paper defines toolkit = templates + presets + seeded flagship + ≤3 blocks + interop answer, all on existing machinery. If the user imagines something more app-like (a per-vertical Studio mode), that is an architecture conversation to have BEFORE wave 3.
  • 5. The pre-resolve doctrine (with the capstone): must every surface render from source, or may the server pre-resolve (freshness stamps, citation formatting, notation layout)? One answer should govern all three lanes' designs.
